Of the seven prior findings: F-53, F-54 and F-57 are closed (decisions.md D-M5S04-06, D-M5S04-05, re-compile note); F-56 is further partially closed (D-M5S04-08); F-52 is partially closed on nine of ten original members but reopened on its narrowest edge by a new orphan (TestUserFactory, added after the addendum was written); F-55 and F-58 are unchanged and still open. findings.title: TestUserFactory is a live, tool-confirmed traceability orphan; F-52 is reopened on its narrowest edge
findings.detail: check_rtm.py's member-to-row orphan direction - the deepening F-52 asked the library to add - is now live (skills/admin/requirements-traceability-matrix v1.1.5, commits 0c585e185/cf9dde917/ef8e10141, all landed after the 2026-09-12T12:52 run). Run against today's artefacts it reports exactly one orphan: ApexClass:TestUserFactory, present in artefacts/M5-S05/package.xml with no row in traceability.md naming it, not even inside an artefact_paths cell. This is not a re-discovery of F-52's original ten: decisions.md D-M5S04-07's addendum still correctly cross-references nine of those ten (the tenth, EmailFolder:case_intake, was always covered via REQ-032). TestUserFactory did not exist when that addendum was compiled (13:15Z) - M4-S05's F-59 repair added it roughly four hours later (~17:00Z) - so the addendum could not have named it. The milestone's declared check_rtm.py test carries no --strict flag and the orphan rule is a WARN regardless of --strict, so the test still exits 0; the gap surfaces only because this run reads the WARN text, not just the exit code.

evidence.grounded_in: python3 skills/admin/requirements-traceability-matrix/scripts/check_rtm.py --file artefacts/M5-S04/traceability.md --manifest-dir artefacts, this run, orphan report naming ApexClass:TestUserFactory (evidenced by M4-S05/classes/TestUserFactory.cls-meta.xml); artefacts/M5-S04/traceability.md's own addendum (does not name TestUserFactory); decisions.md D-M4S05-06 (repair timestamp), D-M5S04-07 (addendum timestamp)

findings.recommendation: Accept as an extension of F-52's known gap; the G5 gate is already approved and this does not reopen it. At the next build-doc-keeper touch on M5-S04 or the next traceability.md write on M4-S05, add TestUserFactory to the existing addendum or to REQ-044's artefact_paths cell (REQ-044 already names the trigger the other three Apex classes serve, and TestUserFactory's fixture exists to prove the same trigger's behaviour). No further checker work needed - the tool already does its job.

findings.title: CWB-OTHER-042's own prose is stale by one member, in the same pattern the original report already named Concerning
findings.detail: artefacts/M5-S04/configuration-workbook.md's row CWB-OTHER-042 (added by the same 13:15Z re-compile that closed F-57) describes artefacts/M5-S05/package.xml as '29 types, 56 members' - true when written, false as of the 18:29Z M5-S05 rebuild that no re-compile has seen since. This is the identical structural cause the original report's section 13 already flagged as Concerning ('the compile ran before the build finished, twice over, in two different severities' - F-54 and F-57), recurring a third time, in the one row whose entire content is a number this re-verification exists to check.

evidence.grounded_in: direct read of CWB-OTHER-042's text ('29 types, 56 members') against artefacts/M5-S05/package.xml's current 57 members, this run

findings.recommendation: No independent action. Folding the CWB-OTHER-042 correction into whatever future compile closes F-63 (which touches the same file) closes this at no extra cost. The number a release owner actually deploys from is artefacts/M5-S05/package.xml itself, read directly, not this compiled description of it.

process_observations.observation: The build's own decisions.md named the exact gap this re-verification exists to close, before any human asked for it, in the last entry written before this run.

scripts/build_plan.py's set-milestone handler already implements a safe re-verification path for an already-accepted milestone: it records the new verdict and report path in a reverifications[] array without moving status away from accepted or touching the gate, so a re-verification cannot accidentally unmake a human approval.

The same structural cause named Concerning in the original report's section 13 - a compile step running before every input that feeds it has landed - produced a second, independently discoverable instance one rebuild later (F-63/F-64), on files the M5-S04 re-compile had just finished repairing for the prior instance of the same cause.

check_rtm.py's orphan rule has no --strict-promotable severity of its own (unlike its coverage-gap rule), so a real, tool-confirmed traceability gap and a routine WARN read identically at the exit-code level; a reviewer who checks only the exit code would not see F-63 at all.

A fresh milestone-verifier pass over M4 would be the natural companion to this one: G4 was re-signed by the operator against the same runs 4-8 this report reads, and decisions.md O-M5S05-01 names that re-pass as still outstanding for M4 specifically.
process_observations.followup_reason: because O-M5S05-01 names the M4 re-pass as the sibling gap this M5 re-verification does not itself close, and it is the same agent's job on the milestone one step earlier
